B2-1-0.title: Gerund after verbs and prepositions

items.t: I enjoy spending time alone.
She avoids arguing with him.
He suggested leaving early.
I enjoy to spend time alone.
She is good at solving problems.
Thanks for helping me.
He left without saying goodbye.
Thanks for to help me.

B2-1-0.note_es: Tras enjoy, avoid, mind, keep y tras cualquier preposición, el verbo siguiente va en -ing, nunca en infinitivo.

B2-1-1.title: Noun clause after be
B2-1-1.note_es: Tras be, una oración entera hace de complemento: define o explica el sujeto.

B2-2-0.title: Past obligation: three structures

items.t: I had to work late on Friday.
We had to show our passports.

columns.head: should have
columns.use_es: Era lo correcto, pero no se hizo.

items.t: You should have called me.
I should have studied more.

columns.head: was supposed to
columns.use_es: Era el plan, pero no ocurrió.

items.t: He was supposed to arrive at six.
We were supposed to meet.

B2-2-0.note_es: Had to = obligación cumplida. Should have y was supposed to = algo esperado que no sucedió.

B2-2-1.point: Modals for degrees of certainty about the past
B2-2-1.title: How sure are you about the past?

marks.ex: He can’t have left; his coat is here.
She might have missed the bus.
They must have forgotten the time.

B2-2-1.note_es: Must have = deducción casi segura; might have = posibilidad; can’t have = deducción de que fue imposible.

B2-3-0.title: Defining vs non-defining clauses

items.t: The man who called is my boss.
The book that I read was long.
The man, who called, is my boss.

columns.head: non-defining
columns.use_es: Solo añade información; no admite that.

items.t: My boss, who called, is away.
Paris, which I love, is huge.
My sister, that lives in Rome, is ill.

B2-3-0.note_es: La cláusula defining identifica y no lleva comas. La non-defining solo añade datos, va entre comas y no usa that.

B2-3-1.title: Adjective order: opinion to material
B2-3-1.note_es: Orden habitual: opinión, tamaño, edad, forma, color, origen, material y luego el nombre.

B2-3-2.title: Despite, although, however

items.t: Despite the rain, we went out.
Despite being tired, he smiled.
Despite it rained, we went out.
Although it rained, we went out.
Although the rain, we went out.

columns.head: however
columns.use_es: Va con coma, entre dos frases.

items.t: It rained. However, we went out.
It rained however we went out.

B2-3-2.note_es: Despite + nombre/-ing; although + oración completa; however conecta dos oraciones y lleva coma.

B2-4-0.title: Reduced time clause
B2-4-0.note_es: Si las dos cláusulas tienen el mismo sujeto, se omite el sujeto y el auxiliar tras while, before o after.

B2-4-1.title: Reason and condition

items.t: I stayed in because it was cold.
Since you’re here, let’s start.
As it was late, we left.
If it rains, we’ll stay in.
Unless you hurry, you’ll be late.
You can go as long as you call.

B2-4-1.note_es: Because, since y as dan la razón. If, unless y as long as dan la condición (unless = if not).

B2-5-0.title: It’s + adjective + to + verb
B2-5-0.note_es: Se comenta una conducta sin culpar a nadie: It’s + adjetivo o nombre + infinitivo con to.

B2-5-1.title: The -ing form as subject
B2-5-1.note_es: Un gerundio puede ser el sujeto de la oración y siempre lleva el verbo en singular.

B2-7-0.title: Tag questions
B2-7-0.note_es: La coletilla repite el auxiliar con signo contrario. Nobody y never cuentan como negativos.

B2-7-1.title: Statement to negative question
B2-7-1.note_es: Se invierte el auxiliar negativo para dar tu opinión y pedir acuerdo: Isn’t it worrying…?

B2-7-2.point: Passive of present continuous, present perfect, future
B2-7-2.title: Present continuous passive
B2-7-2.note_es: Present continuous pasivo: am/is/are + being + participio. El agente obvio se omite.

B2-7-2.point: Passive of present continuous, present perfect, future
B2-7-2.title: Present perfect passive with agent
B2-7-2.note_es: Present perfect pasivo: has/have + been + participio. Usa by solo si el agente importa.

B2-8-0.title: Reduced relative: -ing
B2-8-0.note_es: Se omite who/that + be delante de un -ing: la forma -ing da la acción en curso.

B2-8-0.title: Reduced relative: participle
B2-8-0.note_es: Con voz pasiva se omite that + was y queda el participio pasado.

B2-8-1.title: Which refers to the whole sentence
B2-8-1.note_es: Which tras una coma puede referirse a toda la oración anterior y no solo a un nombre.

B2-9-0.title: Unlike, while, whereas, except that

items.t: Unlike my brother, I hate fish.
Unlike Spain, Norway is cold.
He loves tea, whereas I prefer coffee.
While she saves, he spends.
It was perfect, except that it rained.
I agree, except that it’s costly.

B2-9-0.note_es: Unlike va con un nombre; while, whereas y except that van con una oración completa.

B2-10-0.title: Noun clause vs relative clause

items.t: What annoys me is the noise.
That annoys me is the noise.
The item that broke was cheap.
The item what broke was cheap.

B2-10-0.note_es: What no lleva antecedente (es un nombre en sí). Una relativa modifica un nombre con that, which o who.

B2-10-1.title: Direct to indirect question
B2-10-1.note_es: En la pregunta indirecta el orden es afirmativo: sujeto + verbo, sin inversión ni do.

B2-11-1.title: Three ways to use wish

items.t: I wish I had more time.
I wish I were taller.

columns.head: wish + past perfect
columns.use_es: Pesar por algo que ya pasó.

items.t: I wish I had studied more.
She wishes she hadn’t left.

columns.head: wish + would
columns.use_es: Molestia por la conducta de otro.

items.t: I wish he would stop talking.
I wish it would rain.

B2-11-1.note_es: Wish + pasado = presente irreal; + past perfect = pesar del pasado; + would = queja o cambio deseado.
